A diversified lump sum buy and hold strategy may include U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities.

California is facing an energy crisis characterized by high electricity and natural gas prices, rolling blackouts, and tight supplies. Federal regulators (FERC) have implemented a price-mitigation plan to control the wholesale electricity market, while a special state Senate committee is subpoenaing eight out-of-state power generators, including Enron, to investigate illegal profiteering.

Enron is featured in a PBS "Frontline" documentary regarding the crisis and is involved in several other developments: it is in a pricing dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over the Dabhol Power project in India, it sold its 20% stake in a Saudi Arabian gas venture to USX-Marathon Group, and it is proposing a fuel cell power farm in Connecticut using public conservation funds. Additionally, White House strategist Karl Rove's financial disclosures reveal holdings in Enron.

NeoWorld is a deep learning framework that constructs an infinite, interactive virtual world from a single image. To balance computational efficiency with visual realism, it uses a hybrid object-centric scene structure that represents backgrounds as lightweight 2D surfaces and progressively unfolds foreground objects into full 3D models based on user prompts or camera proximity. 

The pipeline integrates an inverse rendering process using object-centric Gaussian layers, an image-to-3D reconstruction module for object alignment, and a Large Language Model (LLM) to interpret natural language commands for object manipulation and physics-based animation. Experimental results indicate that NeoWorld outperforms prior 2D and 2.5D methods in 3D rendering quality, text-motion alignment, and user engagement.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to address unacceptable delays in delivering performance-based bonuses to public school teachers, which have occurred since school year 2012-2013. Teachers have not yet received bonuses for school year 2016-2017. DepEd Undersecretary Jesus Mateo attributed the delays to failed biddings and clearance processing.

Former president Robert Mugabe returned home from Singapore and Dubai amid allegations from President Emmerson Mnangagwa's administration. Mnangagwa suggested that Mugabe's allies, Generation 40 (G40), were behind a June 24 bomb blast in Bulawayo that killed two and injured over 40 people. Patrick Zhuwao, a G40 member, warned British Prime Minister Theresa May that Mnangagwa might use this "hunch without evidence" to target enemies. Mugabe has called the current administration illegitimate.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system featuring internal clamp protection for inputs up to ±18V, a Programmable Gain Amplifier (PGA), and a common-mode rejection circuit supporting up to ±12V. It includes programmable low-pass filters, a precision internal voltage reference, and a source-synchronous data interface supporting 2-lane or 4-lane SDR/DDR modes. Additional features include a data output randomizer, simple and moving data averaging, and various digital test patterns. The device supports a speed-boost mode for up to 8MSPS on a selected channel pair and can be configured via SPI in single or daisy-chain topologies.

On February 2, 2015, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. to issue $500 million in 2020 Floating Rate Notes and fixed rate notes totaling $6 billion across maturities in 2020, 2022, 2025, and 2045. These senior unsecured obligations were issued pursuant to a 2013 indenture and registration statement.

Researchers developed a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to study the distribution of four first-line anti-TB drugs (rifampicin, ethambutol, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide) at extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) sites, specifically the pleura and lymph nodes. Calibrated and validated using plasma and lung data, the model predicts that rifampicin and isoniazid generally exceed critical concentrations in most organs, while pyrazinamide and ethambutol often fall below these thresholds in various EPTB sites. The study suggests that PBPK modeling can help optimize EPTB treatment regimens.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017, reports total revenue of $24.5 billion and net income of $6.6 billion, compared to $21.9 billion and $5.7 billion for the same period in 2016. The company early adopted new accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases effective July 1, 2017. As of September 30, 2017, total assets were $249.1 billion and total liabilities were $159.5 billion. The company also noted the December 2016 acquisition of LinkedIn for $27.0 billion.

The Federal Open Market Committee increased the federal funds rate by 0.25 points to a 1 to 1.25 percent target area. This follows a March increase to 0.75-1 percent and a December 2015 hike, ending a seven-year period of 0.25 percent rates established after the 2007 financial crisis.

Researchers established the K-T collaborative EVT registry by harmonizing data from South Korea's CRCS-K and Taiwan's TREAT-AIS, totaling 9,941 patients. The study found that Taiwanese patients generally had more severe strokes and complex risk profiles, leading to lower functional recovery rates. While advanced age (particularly 75–85 years) was associated with higher mortality and lower functional independence, it did not significantly increase the risk of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. The findings suggest that while age influences outcomes, carefully selected elderly patients can still benefit from endovascular thrombectomy.
Dr. Maria Pane is a neonatologist at GBMC who uses a cohesive approach to care by including parents in rounds. She also supports the neonatal intensive care unit's Father’s Day 5K fundraiser.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2022. The company reported consolidated net sales of $121.2 billion for Q2 2022, a 7% increase over Q2 2021, though it experienced a net loss of $2.0 billion. This loss was influenced by a $3.9 billion valuation loss from its equity investment in Rivian.

Operating results varied by segment: AWS saw a 33% sales increase and grew operating income to $5.7 billion, while the North America and International segments reported operating losses of $627 million and $1.7 billion, respectively, due to increased fulfillment and transportation costs.

Key corporate activities included a 20-for-1 stock split on May 27, 2022, the acquisition of MGM Holdings Inc. for approximately $6.1 billion on March 17, 2022, and an agreement in July 2022 to acquire 1Life Healthcare, Inc. for approximately $3.9 billion. The company also repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock during the first six months of 2022.

Yael Kalai introduces Probabilistically Checkable Proofs (PCPs), which allow a verifier to check the validity of a proof by querying only a few random locations rather than reading the entire witness. The lecture demonstrates how to construct a PCP for any NP language (specifically 3SAT) by "unrolling" the GKR protocol.

The construction involves creating low-degree extensions of the witness and each layer of the verification circuit, and providing all possible sumcheck protocol transcripts as an oracle. By using specific parameter engineering (setting the field size $F$ to be poly-logarithmic relative to the circuit size $s$), the resulting PCP remains polynomial in size. The verifier simulates the GKR protocol using the oracle, achieving completeness 1 and soundness 1/2 with polylogarithmic randomness and query complexity. The session concludes by noting that while GKR handles most soundness, a low-degree test is required for the input layer since the verifier does not possess the witness.

This study investigated the impact of mydriasis (pupil dilation) on the gradability of retinal images and the performance of an AI model for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening using the Phelcom Eyer portable camera. Analyzing 327 patients, researchers found that mydriatic images had a significantly higher gradability rate (82.1%) than non-mydriatic images (55.6%). In the non-mydriatic group, lower image quality was significantly associated with male gender, older age, longer diabetes duration, systemic hypertension, and Indigenous race. The AI model performed better with mydriatic images, achieving higher accuracy (82.91% vs. 79.23%), F1 score, and AUC, as well as a lower false positive rate. While non-mydriatic imaging is more pragmatic for resource-limited settings, the results suggest mydriasis enhances diagnostic precision and reduces overdiagnosis.

A Stephens County jury convicted Robert Pearl Bryson of two counts of aggravated sodomy, four counts of aggravated child molestation, one count of child molestation, and two counts of failure to register as a sex offender. Bryson appealed, challenging the sufficiency of the evidence, the denial of motions to quash the indictment, the denial of his counsel's motion to withdraw, the denial of a motion to sever charges, the admission of a no contest plea, and the effectiveness of his trial counsel. The court found no error and affirmed the convictions, ruling that the evidence was sufficient, the trial court did not abuse its discretion regarding counsel or severance, the plea was admissible, and Bryson had waived his claim of ineffective assistance.

The authors propose Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), a framework designed to scale image registration to ultra-high-resolution biomedical images. To address memory and compute bottlenecks, the framework introduces fused CUDA kernels for a composite implicit grid sampler, implicit Parzen windowing for Mutual Information (MI), and fused Local Normalized Cross-Correlation (LNCC). Additionally, FFDP employs "Grid Parallel" (GP) for boundary-synchronized sharding and a distributed ring sampler to handle large moving images across multiple GPUs.

Experimental results demonstrate that FFDP accelerates traditional registration pipelines by up to 7.48× and deep learning pipelines by up to 6.14×, while significantly reducing memory consumption. The authors successfully registered a multimodal human brain volume with over 11.8B parameters in one minute using 8 GPUs. Comparative analysis on a simulated 250µm dataset shows that FFDP outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning and distributed baselines in both accuracy and efficiency.

This research develops a multidimensional data-driven AI innovation taxonomy framework to help enterprises manage the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA). Using a combination of literature reviews and expert interviews, the author creates an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain and a five-level maturity framework ranging from "Human Led/Initial Analytics" to "Machine Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV." The study aims to provide a strategic tool for identifying automation use cases and managing human-machine interactions within digital business platforms.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 has several technical issues:

*   **SSMI/IRQ:** Simultaneous events may cause I/O to complete before the SSMI is signaled.
*   **UDMA/IDE:** UDMA fails if the bus master is enabled before the PIO command packet. Additionally, certain CD-ROM drive interrupts can reset the bus master engine.
*   **Power/Wake:** Most wake inputs fail in ACPI S3 state; use PWRBTN# instead. Sleep_X may not deassert if delay counters exceed the PM_SED delay.
*   **RAM/DMA:** RTC CMOS RAM reads can be incorrect if following extended data port writes. Block and demand mode legacy DMA to LPC can return invalid data.
*   **USB/LPC/SMB:** USB clock gating causes register read failures. LPC controllers may abort transactions with specific SYNC patterns. The SMB controller's NEGACK bit may be cleared incorrectly or set slowly.
*   **Other:** ATAC may hang if PRD addresses are not DWORD aligned. The GLPCI retry counter includes all PCI bus retries. Atomic writes to GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Registers after suspend clear non-selected bits. The LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to set after abnormal standby.

The Supreme Court of Mississippi affirmed the second manslaughter conviction of Ulysses S. Gandy, who was sentenced to ten years in prison following a fatal two-car collision. The court found sufficient evidence to support the jury's conclusion that Gandy was intoxicated and drove into the wrong lane of traffic, constituting culpable negligence. The court further ruled that the trial court did not commit reversible error in refusing a specific intoxication instruction, admitting sketches used to illustrate the scene as observed by witnesses, or denying a jury recess for refreshments.

Researchers developed a meta-population model to analyze how Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) correlate with SARS-CoV-2 transmission in Norway, Sweden, and Germany. The model treats activity in four settings—Workplaces, Transit stations, Retail & recreation, and Grocery & pharmacy—as additive contributors to transmissibility, while modeling temperature (seasonality) and virus variants (Alpha and Delta) as multiplicative factors.

Findings indicate that GCMR data reflect population behavior related to infection dynamics. In Sweden, 60% of infections were attributed to the four GCMR settings, compared to 38.7% in Norway. In Norway and Sweden, Transit stations and Workplaces were the most significant settings for transmission. Conversely, in Berlin and Bavaria, Retail & recreation was the most influential setting. The model also estimated that a 20°C temperature increase reduces transmissibility by approximately 40-50%, and the Delta variant roughly doubles transmissibility compared to the wildtype.

Accepting the presidential nomination, the speaker contrasts his vision of hope and growth with his opponents' "government of pessimism." He criticizes the opposition's history of high inflation, taxes, and deficits, while citing his own achievements in economic growth, job creation, and military strengthening. He advocates for limited government, individual liberty, and a balanced budget amendment.

EUR/USD is rising toward daily highs around 1.1840, supported by a weakening US dollar following Friday's inflation figures. Market participants are awaiting ECB and FOMC minutes regarding QE tapering and balance sheet reduction. Key resistance levels are 1.1846, 1.1894, and 1.1911, while support levels include 1.1722, 1.1687, and 1.1611.

Texas Instruments warns that integrated circuits can be damaged by ESD, potentially causing performance degradation or device failure. Revision A (May 2025) updated the status of ADS8685W and ADS8689W to Production Data. The document provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, alongside legal disclaimers regarding data accuracy, warranties, and user responsibility.

Reports from July 2001 indicate that California's energy crisis involved various wholesale merchants; some public entities charged the state more per megawatt-hour than private firms like Enron, Dynegy, Duke Energy, and Mirant. Meanwhile, a Senate committee probed Duke Energy for suspected price gouging, and mediation between California and power generators failed to reach an agreement on $8.9 billion in demanded refunds.

In India, Enron's Dabhol Power Company CEO Neil McGregor resigned. Chairman Kenneth Lay met with Indian officials to discuss a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, which halted construction on the project's second phase. Additionally, Enron Broadband Services invested in Tropic Networks' $60-million financing. Despite various legal and international challenges, some analysts maintained a "buy" rating for Enron stock.

Grief is a unique, personal emotional reaction to the loss of a person, object, or life circumstance. It can occur in advance of a loss (anticipatory grief) or result from events like illness, retirement, or moving home. The grieving process is complex and variable, potentially involving numbness, denial, relief, yearning, restlessness, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and depression. While the duration of grief varies, most people eventually learn to cope and make necessary life adjustments.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system featuring a built-in analog front-end. It supports simple and moving data averaging to improve SNR, as well as fixed, digital ramp, and alternating test patterns for debugging. The device includes a speed-boost mode for sampling a selected channel pair up to 8MSPS and offers low-noise or wide-bandwidth modes. Configuration is managed via SPI, supporting single-device or daisy-chain topologies across three register banks. Power-down and reset are controlled via dedicated pins or register writes.

The New England Patriots lost to the Miami Dolphins following a poor offensive performance, including 0-11 third-down conversions. A failed onside kick by Stephen Gostkowski in the final minute ended the Patriots' chance to tie the game.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell have improved hyperlensing capabilities by using isotopically purified boron to create hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) crystals. This isotopic engineering reduces optical losses and increases polariton lifetime, enhancing imaging resolution by approximately a factor of ten. This allows for the potential imaging of objects as small as 30 nanometers, such as viruses, in their natural environments using non-harmful infrared light. This advance may impact biological science, medical science, communications, and nanoscale optical components.

To beat an offside trap, attackers must recognize the trap, adjust their play to remain onside, and utilize the space behind defenders. Tactics include dribbling through, using through passes, horizontal, checking, bending, or delayed runs, and employing short, back, or square passes. Attackers may also use a designated "non-runner" or fakes during free kicks. Success results in a one-on-one opportunity with the goalkeeper and may discourage the opposing team from using the trap again.

Ocean acidification harms calcifying organisms like coral reefs and oysters by reducing available carbonate ions. However, research published in Environmental Science & Technology shows that periwinkles can adapt to predicted 2100 pH levels by producing less-dense inner shells and more soluble-resistant shells, despite a declined metabolism.
In the case of People v. Roldán, the court reversed the judgment and acquitted the defendant based on the grounds and evidence from the similar case of People v. Soldán.

China's Ministry of Commerce blacklisted TechInsights and nine subsidiaries, placing them on an "unreliable entity list" and banning business with Chinese organizations. This follows a TechInsights report suggesting Huawei's AI chips used international components, which China claims violated national interests and endangered national security. The ban prohibits Chinese entities from collaborating with the firm, restricting its access to the Chinese market.

Jack Hough of Barron's suggests Netflix could lose over half its value due to competition from Disney, Facebook, and Amazon, as well as its accounting and cash-burning practices. Conversely, others argue Netflix's growth despite existing competition, its ability to raise prices, and its market dominance create a moat that protects the company.

A study in the journal Pediatrics found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 children under 6 were treated for window-blind injuries. While most injuries were minor, cord entanglement caused nearly 80% of hospitalizations and over 94% of deaths. Dr. Gary Smith and Linda Kaiser advocate for mandatory standards to eliminate accessible cords. Currently, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission is in the first stage of mandatory rulemaking, while the Window Covering Manufacturers Association has proposed updating voluntary standards for "stock" products.

Ryan Kerr, 26, was remanded in custody by Taunton Crown Court after admitting to multiple attacks. These included brawling with a love rival, punching the rival's mother, and stamping on a man at The George Hotel. Judge David Ticehurst will determine the sentence on October 13.

Peterborough City Council pledged £4 million for homeless families and brought 179 empty homes back into use last year, totaling 663 over five years. The council published Phase Two budget proposals amid government grant cuts from £55 million to £10 million over eight years. Additionally, Public Space Protection Orders have reduced anti-social behavior, and the CHUMS service has launched to support youth mental health.

Chef and cookbook author Shannon Bard announced the permanent closure of her Portland restaurant, Zapoteca, to spend more time with her children. Bard and her husband, Tom, still own two restaurants in Kennebunk, a cooking school, and a catering company.

The DAWN study evaluated the efficacy and safety of combining best supportive care with high-volume, high-neutralizing-antibody-titer convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The primary objective was to assess clinical efficacy and safety, while the secondary objective focused on clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, requiring IEC approval and signed informed consent from participants.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures the average US Equity market exposure reported by its members via weekly surveys. Used to estimate investor sentiment, high readings suggest bullishness and low readings suggest bearishness, potentially serving as a contrarian indicator. However, the index is not predictive, and backtests indicate it performs poorly as a trading strategy compared to other indicators like the VIX.

Lubrizol Corp. is investing US$80 million to expand its engineered polymers thermoplastics polyurethane (TPU) production capacity and technology across North America, Europe, and Asia to meet increased demand. This includes new capabilities in North America, new lines in Songjiang, China, and extended production for elastomers, aliphatics, and adhesives in Europe.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane. Promoter Bob Arum stated a Horn victory could lead to fights with Terence Crawford or Manny Pacquiao in 2018. The matchup follows accusations from Corcoran's camp regarding Horn's head-butting and claims from Corcoran about biting.

President Trump announced a deal with Pfizer to lower drug prices for patients and the Medicaid program, with new medicines priced at parity with other countries. In exchange for continued U.S. manufacturing investment, Pfizer will avoid certain import tariffs. While Trump plans further deals with other companies, policy experts are skeptical about the agreement's actual impact on drug affordability. Additionally, Sanofi is being investigated by the European Commission for potentially anticompetitive activity.

Manchester City faces Burnley at the Etihad Stadium on Jan. 2 at 10:00 AM ET. City aims to maintain an unbeaten run and title charge, while Burnley seeks points to avoid relegation. City will rely on Sergio Aguero, Kevin de Bruyne, and David Silva, while Burnley's threats include Andre Gray and Sam Vokes.

This study compared EEG responses to median nerve electrical stimulation between adults with Tourette syndrome (TS) and healthy controls to investigate "neural noise." Results showed that the TS group had significantly increased trial-by-trial variability and flatter 1/f noise slopes at beta and gamma frequencies, suggesting less stable neuronal recruitment at rest. However, this variability normalized in response to stimulation, with both groups showing similar reductions in the coefficient of variation. Additionally, the TS group exhibited a significantly increased P2 (P100) SEP component, which correlated with tic severity and may relate to tactile hypersensitivity.

Facebook has released a detailed version of its community standards to provide transparency regarding permitted content on subjects like hate speech, drug use, and violence. The company now allows appeals for individual content removals and provides specific reasons for takedowns. Facebook employs 7,500 moderators and uses automated software to enforce these evolving rules, which are reviewed biweekly.
On June 20, 2017, Apple Inc. consummated the issuance and sale of $1,000,000,000 in 3.000% senior unsecured Notes due June 20, 2027. Interest will be paid semi-annually starting December 20, 2017.

A federal jury unanimously cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive force accusations. Jon "Chris" Erwin alleged Hudson used unreasonable force when punching him seven times and throwing him to the ground outside a restaurant in October 2011. The jury decided the force used was reasonable from Hudson's perspective. The city of Little Rock and the restaurant's owner settled Erwin's claims before the trial.

The Finnish press largely ignored U.S. war statements and attacked the U.S. administration, likely due to German influence and Finland's dependence on Germany for food and military supplies. Internally, Finland faced growing war weariness, social division between Socialists and Conservatives, and public impatience with the occupation of Soviet Karelia. Meanwhile, U.S. officials warned Finland that press attacks on the U.S. could jeopardize future diplomatic support.

Under the leadership of Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, Enron transformed from a pipeline company into a dominant energy trading colossus. Skilling implemented a high-pressure, merit-based culture characterized by "rank and yank" performance reviews and aggressive "mark-to-market" accounting. Despite massive growth and expansion into broadband and water, the company eventually faced declining stock prices, accounting scrutiny, and failures in its telecommunications and international projects. Jeff Skilling resigned as CEO in 2001 after a short tenure, citing a need for personal time.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported a 43% increase in consolidated net sales for the first quarter of 2018, reaching $51.042 billion, with net income rising to $1.629 billion. Growth was driven by increased unit sales in North America and International segments, and increased customer usage in AWS. The company acquired Ring Inc. on April 12, 2018, for approximately $900 million. As of March 31, 2018, total assets were $126.362 billion and total stockholders' equity was $31.463 billion.

The speaker discusses a series where frequent penalties have disrupted the flow and made it difficult to establish a style of play. To improve, the team must increase quickness in the neutral zone and defensive positioning. The speaker notes the opponent's strong penalty kill and describes how restructuring the defense to play to individual strengths improved team structure. Additionally, the speaker addresses coaching philosophy, emphasizing adaptation, delegation to staff, and a passion for the game.

This work addresses the challenge of capturing dynamic material transformations in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) by identifying reusable Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs). The authors defined three core requirements for process modeling: process structure, data and resources, and project goals/participant roles. 

They analyzed several ontologies, finding that PMDcore supports all three requirements, while others like P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW, WILD, and GPO provide partial support. Additionally, the authors developed a baseline method for automated ODP extraction using semantic similarity techniques and the ROBOT framework. Evaluation results indicate that while semantic similarity can identify relevant patterns, the method is currently biased by annotation quality and requirement formulation. Future work aims to integrate ontology mappings and develop a platform to publish extracted patterns for the MSE community.

Florida State linebacker Ethan Pritchard was released from Tallahassee Memorial Hospital and moved to Brooks Rehabilitation in Jacksonville. Pritchard was shot in the back of the head on August 31 in a case of mistaken identity; four people have been arrested. Florida State reports that Pritchard is alert, responsive, and able to communicate.

Old Forge High School students Christian Killino, Iain Kerrigan, and Kole Barbetti raised $3,864 for St. Jude’s Research Hospital through a Math-a-thon senior project. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary, with a new board appointed for two years. The auxiliary has scheduled two fundraisers: Attic Treasures on July 14-15 and the Best of the Eagles Concert on September 23. Additionally, Hannah Perry Burgess presented a program on honey bee conservation to the Scranton City Chapter of the DAR.

GoDaddy gave the neo-Nazi website The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain for violating terms of service after the site mocked Heather Heyer, a victim of a violent attack in Charlottesville. While the site's publisher, Andrew Anglin, and contributor Andrew Auernheimer responded to the move, Auernheimer noted they have an alternate domain. The Daily Stormer is known for harassment campaigns and has previously been banned by PayPal and a Ukrainian advertising company.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated a Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak involving 22 symptomatic cases linked to an Eid al-Adha celebration in Cardiff. A cohort and case-control study identified "marrara," a traditional raw liver dish, as the most likely vehicle for infection. Whole genome sequencing showed that human isolates were genetically indistinguishable from samples taken from raw lamb, local butchers, and a supplying abattoir. The outbreak resulted in significant illness, with 54% of cases seeking emergency care. In response, Public Health Wales implemented culturally sensitive food safety communications and educational sessions for the community.

An appeals court ruled that the federal government cannot legally ban the interstate trade of Burmese pythons and other giant exotic snakes within the continental U.S., as the Lacey Act only allows restrictions between the continental U.S. and Hawaii or other territories. The ruling does not affect import bans or state laws.

A coach discusses a recent game against New Jersey, noting that a slower pace and better puck possession helped his team gain confidence and transition more effectively. Despite this, he believes the team has lacked a competitive edge for much of the series. He emphasizes that winning the next game requires outplaying New Jersey in more areas and managing the high emotional intensity of the series.

The author warns that neglecting family life and willful sterility threaten the nation. Additionally, the author urges Congress to develop American shipping, specifically suggesting fast mail lines to South America. Finally, the author calls for currency law reform to prevent business disasters caused by interest rate fluctuations during crop seasons, suggesting a plan where national banks issue notes to meet emergencies.

Fad diets are not a healthy or sustainable way to lose weight. Dietician Bonnie Taub-Dix suggests a non-diet approach focused on moderation, establishing a healthy relationship with the body, and promoting long-term healthy habits rather than restriction.
The Gold Coast Titans signed veteran fullback Michael Gordon to a two-year NRL deal after he was released from the Sydney Roosters. Gordon replaces Jarryd Hayne, who left for Parramatta.

Morgan McSweeney, a biotech professional and Ph.D. in pharmaceutical sciences and immunology known as "Dr. Noc," uses social media to provide "edutainment" on public health. He focuses on making complex science digestible and actionable for a general audience, often using reaction videos to debunk misinformation. McSweeney emphasizes the importance of nuance and personal relatability to build trust with viewers, noting that institutional communication often lacks this human element. He maintains a separate professional life in drug development and advocates for more diverse experts to create evidence-based content to counter the prevalence of wellness misinformation.

Devised by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965, the Coppock Curve is a long-term momentum indicator used primarily for stocks and indices to identify market swings. It is calculated as a 10-month Weighted Moving Average (WMA) of the sum of 11-month and 14-month Rate of Change (ROC) indicators. Long entries are triggered when the curve crosses above the zero line, and exits occur when it crosses below. Backtesting on a monthly time frame shows the strategy can reduce drawdowns and risk-adjusted returns may exceed a buy-and-hold strategy.

Nick Foles, a backup quarterback, is leading the Philadelphia Eagles toward Super Bowl LII after Carson Wentz suffered a torn ACL. While Wentz is expected to return as the starter in 2018, Foles' success may lead to a trade to another team or his retention as a backup.

Addressing the 100th Congress, the President highlighted economic improvements, including lower inflation and unemployment. He accepted responsibility for a failed action in Iran and urged continued support for defense and freedom, specifically regarding the Soviet Union, Afghanistan, and Nicaragua. He proposed a balanced budget amendment, a line-item veto, welfare reform, and legislation for elderly catastrophic illness. Additionally, he called for increased national competitiveness through science, technology, and education reform, while advocating for voluntary prayer in schools.

The TMS320DM814x memory map includes L4 Fast and Slow Peripheral Domains, with certain L4 Slow regions reserved for masters other than the Cortex-A8. The TILER provides an additional 4-GBytes of addressing for rotated and mirrored frame buffer views, accessible primarily by the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems. Terminal functions tables detail pin assignments, multiplexing, and electrical characteristics. Specifically, BTMODE pins are sampled at reset to determine ARM Cortex-A8 boot configurations and GPMC settings before functioning as GPMC multiplexed data/address pins.

The speaker emphasizes the need for the team to work hard, play for each other, and avoid being outworked. He notes a lack of collective effort in a Stanley Cup final game and stresses the importance of getting more shots on net and improving synchronization between passing and shooting.

The NDSU Faculty Senate sent a draft resolution to all 11 North Dakota University System campuses declaring a "crisis of confidence" caused by budget cuts, consolidation, and a lack of support from the NDUS and State Board of Higher Education. The resolution calls for "supportive collaborations" and a Higher Education Summit with state leadership to ensure institutions can fulfill their missions. UND campus senate chair Dana Harsell stated the executive committee will discuss the proposal to determine if the wider body supports it.

The author wrote this book to provide a shared language and collection of repeatable, generic patterns for building reliable distributed systems. This aims to make development more efficient and approachable, leveraging containers and orchestrators to avoid the time-consuming reimplementation of common components.

The Energy Central Research Reports Watch is a bi-weekly email newsletter providing power industry research. The February 20, 2002, edition lists recently published reports and white papers from publishers including Minsight Limited, Market Development Group, Datamonitor, SCIENTECH, Inc., and Energy Info Source, Inc. These reports cover utility industry profiles, company data, and market trends.

This lecture discusses the business case for sustainable real estate, focusing on the intersection of capital markets and the space market. The instructor explains that sustainable buildings (green, healthy, and climate-resilient) can command rental premiums due to lower operational costs and better quality, which translates to higher purchase prices and returns for owners and developers.

The session introduces "sustainable finance," where climate risk is treated as financial risk. Using portfolio theory, the instructor illustrates how green buildings—characterized by lower risk and higher potential returns—can shift the efficient frontier, attracting more capital than "brown" (conventional) buildings.

Regarding debt, the lecture covers how climate risks, such as wildfires and flooding, increase default risks for mortgages, particularly in low-income areas. Conversely, "green mortgages" may offer lower interest rates or higher loan-to-value ratios because energy-efficient homes typically have lower default rates and lower monthly utility costs. Finally, the instructor touches upon private equity, noting that firms are increasingly incorporating ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) criteria into investment memos to align social value with business returns.

This work proposes a theoretical framework for information design that integrates behavioral framing effects with the classic Bayesian persuasion model. While traditional models focus on quantitative correlations between signals and world states, this model incorporates a "belief oracle"—approximated by Large Language Models (LLMs)—to map natural language framings to receiver beliefs.

The authors identify three optimization variants for the sender: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint framing and recommendation. Theoretical analysis reveals that framing-only optimization is NP-hard and sensitive to oracle errors due to utility discontinuity. Conversely, joint optimization is more tractable, exhibiting continuity and allowing for a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS).

Empirically, the authors implement a hill-climbing approach using LLMs and analytical methods. Case studies involving a realtor and a clothing brand demonstrate the method's efficacy, with human evaluations confirming that the model's predictions are directionally correct.

The passage describes several container and distributed system design patterns:

**Single-Node Patterns**
The adapter pattern uses a modular container to modify an application's interface to meet predefined standards. This is particularly useful for normalizing heterogeneous logging and monitoring formats (e.g., using Prometheus or Fluentd) and implementing rich health checks without modifying the original application image.

**Multi-Node Distributed Patterns**
*   **Replicated Load-Balanced Services:** Stateless services are replicated for redundancy and scaling, using load balancers and readiness probes to manage traffic. This can be enhanced with session tracking (via consistent hashing), caching layers (e.g., Varnish), and SSL termination (e.g., nginx).
*   **Sharded Services:** Used for stateful services where data is too large for one machine. A root node distributes requests to specific shards. To improve reliability and handle "hot shards," shards can be replicated.
*   **Scatter/Gather:** This pattern achieves parallelism by farming requests to all leaf nodes simultaneously, with the root combining the partial results. It is used for tasks like distributed document search but is susceptible to the "straggler problem," where the slowest node determines overall latency.

**Functions as a Service (FaaS)**
FaaS enables event-driven, serverless computing. While it simplifies deployment and scaling, it introduces operational challenges regarding monitoring and state management. Key applications include the decorator pattern for request/response transformation and asynchronous event handling, such as two-factor authentication.

The professor discusses the second-order wave equation, exploring its representation as both a second-order equation and a first-order symmetric system with eigenvalues $c$ and $-c$. The lecture covers the continuous solution, noting that waves travel in both directions along characteristic lines.

The professor then analyzes numerical methods:
*   **Semidiscrete (Method of Lines):** Discretizing space while keeping time continuous introduces dispersion, where different frequencies travel at different speeds.
*   **Fully Discrete:** Using second differences in both space and time leads to a quadratic equation for the growth factor $g$. Stability is achieved when the Courrant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition is met ($r < 1$), ensuring the numerical domain of dependence stays within the characteristics.

The session concludes by mentioning that future lectures will cover staggered grids, a common technique in electromagnetism.

This application describes techniques for enhancing "trick-play" (fast-forward and rewind) modes for streamed video. To reduce latency and avoid streaming entire content portions, a media guidance application or trick-play optimizer maintains a "normal buffer window" of continuous video and a "trick-play window" containing only a subset of selected video frames (typically key frames) spaced at intervals.

The system uses metadata, such as frame address information and jump points, to identify and request these specific frames from a server or proxy server. The selection of frames, their quality, and the target buffer sizes are dynamically adjusted based on streaming performance metrics and playback rates. The video player emulates high-speed playback by displaying these sampled frames, adjusting the display rate to match available buffer granularity. Additionally, the system can expand the normal buffer window by requesting intervening frames between previously buffered trick-play frames.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK. Lumps can vary in size and texture, appearing in the breasts or armpits. Warning signs include skin dimpling, redness, rashes, and nipple changes. Risk factors include combined HRT used over five years, genetic mutations (BRCA1/BRCA2), early menstruation, late menopause, and not having children. Risk can be reduced through active lifestyles, healthy weight, and breastfeeding. Men can also develop breast cancer, primarily as lumps or nipple changes. Early detection through self-exams and screening improves survival rates.

Security measures include deploying 1,000 additional officers, increasing undercover personnel, and coordinating with high-rise building employees. Mayor Rahm Emanuel expressed confidence in the city's security plans.
AI models Evo 1 and Evo 2 generated multiple bacteriophage genomes from scratch, some of which outperformed a well-studied strain in lab dishes.

Starting in October, Saudi Aramco will change the formula for its long-term crude oil sales to Asia for the first time since the mid-1980s. The new formula will use a 50:50 average of DME Oman crude futures and S&P Global Platts Dubai cash prices. This move is expected to boost liquidity for Oman futures trading on the DME.

DoorDash has unveiled "Dot," a five-foot-tall autonomous delivery robot equipped with nine cameras and seven sensors. Designed to operate on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes, Dot is part of DoorDash's goal to implement a hybrid delivery model using humans, drones, and autonomous vehicles. While DoorDash also partners with Coco Robotics for smaller sidewalk robots, Dot was developed in-house by DoorDash Labs. The industry faces ongoing challenges regarding navigation, regulation, and human interaction, leading some companies to focus deployments on university campuses or suburbs.

The speaker welcomes a visiting delegation, emphasizing a desire for peace and the protection of their lands through established laws. He expresses willingness to purchase lands on the Mississippi to support boat travel and New Orleans, though specific boundaries must be negotiated on-site. He denies responsibility for unpaid debts from previous English land purchases, citing custom and witness accounts. Additionally, he encourages the visitors to adopt agriculture and industry over hunting and confirms that previously sent goods were gifts. Finally, he arranges for their travel within the country and their eventual return home.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida reversed a Unemployment Appeals Commission order denying Genel Altimeaux unemployment benefits. The appeals referee had determined Altimeaux voluntarily quit his job at Ocean Construction based on testimony from a supervisor, Bruce Milliken, given at a hearing where Altimeaux was absent and unable to conduct cross-examination. The court found this testimony incompetent under Florida law. Testimony from a second hearing did not support the finding that Altimeaux quit, as witness William Tranowski admitted he never personally heard Altimeaux quit, and Altimeaux denied doing so. The court ruled the decision lacked competent, substantial evidence and ordered the reinstatement of Altimeaux's benefits.

Some parents are questioning the transparency and composition of the stakeholder interview committee used by Township High School District 113 to hire a new Highland Park High School principal. Superintendent Christopher Dignam is using Ray and Associates to find a replacement for Tom Koulentes, who leaves June 30.

Pin and Pull is a perimeter run play that uses down block angles to place lead blockers in space. Its strengths include versatility and the ability to get extra blockers to the point of attack. However, it requires a speed-oriented tailback and at least two guards capable of pulling. Unlike the Buck Sweep, which requires a simultaneous inside run threat, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. Variations include the Pin and Pull Toss and the TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss.

Researchers used biologgers with accelerometers, magnetometers, and altimeters to discover that the greater noctule bat hunts migrating songbirds. The bats ascend above 1,200 meters and perform vertically downward sprints to capture prey. Audio recordings captured feeding buzzes and bird distress calls, while DNA analysis and physical evidence confirmed the bats dismember and consume birds in flight.

Gold rallied and the USD Index declined on Friday, but mining stocks and silver failed to move higher. The author suggests the USD Index is poised for a further rally and that stocks may decline significantly. The current market conditions are compared to 2008.

Verizon and AST SpaceMobile have entered a commercial agreement to provide space-based cellular broadband across the continental US. The author rates Verizon as a "strong buy" due to its financial outlook and competitive positioning, while rating AST SpaceMobile as a "sell" because of its high valuation, minimal revenue, and dilution.

Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli is poised to return to power after winning his parliamentary seat, with his Communist UML party and Maoist allies likely to secure a majority. Oli aims to lead a stable five-year government focused on infrastructure projects and foreign investment.

Brock University researchers found that rosemary extract inhibits the growth, survival, and spread of aggressive lung cancer cells. The extract blocks the Akt signalling pathway and enhances apoptosis. Further study is needed to determine which specific polyphenols in rosemary are responsible for these effects.

Plans for a 32-mile "smart motorway" between London and Theale on the M4 (junctions 3 to 12) will be displayed before work begins in September. The £862.4m project involves widening the road to four lanes in both directions, rebuilding eleven bridges, and widening four others. Expected to finish by March 2022, the project aims to reduce congestion for 130,000 daily vehicles using technology to vary speed limits. To address RAC safety concerns regarding the lack of a hard shoulder, Highways England will provide safety areas every 1.12 miles on average.

Enron Corp. filed for bankruptcy in December 2001 following the discovery of massive accounting irregularities and the use of off-balance-sheet partnerships to hide debt and inflate profits. One such venture, "Project Braveheart," involved a failed partnership with Blockbuster Inc. and the fraudulent booking of $110.9 million in profits.

Investigations by the Justice Department, SEC, and Congress are examining Enron's board, which waived ethics codes for executives, and its auditor, Arthur Andersen LLP. Andersen is under scrutiny for allegedly destroying documents and ignoring warnings from whistleblower Sherron Watkins. Other firms, including McKinsey, PricewaterhouseCoopers, and KPMG, are also linked to the collapse.

The scandal has prompted government reviews of retirement-plan security and scrutiny of the Bush administration's ties to Enron. Meanwhile, Enron's European assets are being liquidated or acquired, such as the sale of Enron Nordic Energy to American Electric Power.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces several advancements:

*   **Hardware:** GDDR6X memory provides up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. The architecture features second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores, doubling performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI.
*   **RTX IO:** This technology offloads asset loading and lossless decompression from the CPU to the GPU via Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O performance by up to 100x.
*   **Video Processing:** GA10x GPUs include the fifth-generation NVDEC for hardware-accelerated decoding (including first-time AV1 support) and seventh-generation NVENC for high-quality encoding.
*   **Display & Memory:** Support for HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a enables 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature improves GDDR6X overclocking stability.
*   **Products:** The GeForce RTX 3090 and 3070 target gamers and creators. The A40 and RTX A6000 provide high-performance visual computing for data centers and workstations, featuring scalable memory via NVLink.

COTUTOR is a generative AI educational model that integrates knowledge tracing, signal processing, and convex optimization to provide personalized learning and resource allocation. Unlike traditional LLM-based tools, COTUTOR uses an iterative "flywheel" mechanism to collect multimodal learning signals—such as submission data, participation logs, and queries—to continuously update a probabilistic model of a student's skill mastery.

A key innovation is the use of convex optimization to determine optimal resource allocation, which ensures interpretability, global optimality, and computational efficiency. Implemented as an interactive AI copilot, COTUTOR provides proactive reminders, query resolution, and tailored resource recommendations. Evaluation through benchmarking and classroom studies indicates that COTUTOR outperforms baseline methods in estimating learning states and enhancing student outcomes.
BioNTech SE published a slide deck for a special call regarding InstaDeep Ltd.

Dynegy Inc. is pursuing an all-stock acquisition of Enron Corp. valued at approximately $9.2 billion to $23 billion (including assumed debt). While Dynegy remains optimistic, Enron's stock has plummeted due to a financial scandal involving off-balance-sheet partnerships and earnings restatements, leading to an SEC investigation. To avoid collapse, Enron is seeking $500 million to $1 billion in additional capital from lenders and private equity firms. Dynegy's agreement includes "material adverse change" clauses and specific liability triggers that could allow it to renegotiate or terminate the deal. Additionally, California officials are examining the merger for potential antitrust violations.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon states that while some asset prices are in "bubble territory," AI technology is real and transformative. He warns that AI will eliminate jobs and urges government and business to implement retraining or income solutions to avoid social unrest. Dimon distinguishes between specific AI applications, which he says work for JPMorgan, and generative AI, which he views as more anecdotal. He advises executives to adopt AI and invest in training while calling for thoughtful regulation and safety nets.

Jane Goodall, who died on October 1 at age 91, collected chimpanzee skeletons from Tanzania’s Gombe National Park to ensure nothing was wasted. Because the sex, age, weight, and life experiences of these individuals were known, researchers could study how individual development influences skeletal features, offering a perspective not possible with ancient hominid fossils. For example, the skeleton of a matriarch named Flo demonstrated the difficulty of estimating body weight from bone size and provided insights into skeletal strength and aging in female chimps.

Evgeny Ananiev of VTB Capital JSC predicts gold prices will reach $1,400 an ounce by year-end, driven by U.S.-North Korea tensions and demand from China and India. Analysts note that subdued U.S. inflation and a softened Federal Reserve stance further support prices. Additionally, Indian jewelry consumption and Chinese gold bar demand are rising.

A Business Insider reporter stayed in the Aurora Suite, the cheapest room at approximately $860, at Villa Casa Casuarina (the Versace Mansion) in Miami's South Beach. The reporter described the luxurious suite's decor, a high-end shower, and the hotel's 24k gold tile pool. The experience included attentive staff, access to a rooftop deck and observatory, and a complimentary breakfast.

This application describes multi-camera imaging systems designed to detect faint objects in low-light or low-contrast environments using arrays of economical, low-performance cameras. By co-registering and combining images from $N$ cameras, the system increases the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by at least $\sqrt{N}$ and enhances effective bit depth by approximately $\log_2(N)$. This approach reduces costs, minimizes cosmic ray artifacts, and enables advanced deconvolution.

The system features three array configurations:
*   **Common Field Array:** Multiple cameras share a common field of view region to generate a high-SNR combined image.
*   **Hybrid Field Array:** Multiple common field arrays with overlapping regions are stitched together to create a wide-field composite image with enhanced SNR.
*   **Adaptive Field Array:** Cameras initially form a wide composite field to detect targets, then automatically reconfigure into a common field array to image the target with high sensitivity.

The system includes a computing device for image processing and may utilize calibration, star matching, and data reduction processes (such as Hough transforms) to identify and determine the orbits of uncorrelated space objects.

Asian shares were mostly lower on Wednesday following a U.S. stock sell-off that ended a three-day winning streak. While major indices in Japan, China, Hong Kong, South Korea, and Australia fell, shares rose in Taiwan and Southeast Asia. Meanwhile, the U.S. and China prepare for reciprocal tariffs on $34 billion of imports and exports. Additionally, People's Bank of China Gov. Yi Gang stated that financial risks and currency flows are stable.

The Student Finance Board funded three dance-centered events: the Inter-Greek Council's AirBand, the Asian American Association's Mystique of the East 2017, and the Swing Dance Club's Once Upon A Rock Step. The board also funded its own Summer Training Retreat. Funding was denied for the Association of Students for Africa's Akwaaba Banquet and the Unified Greek Council's Stroll for a Cure due to high costs per student. A request for A Taste of South America was tabled over food costs and potential charitable funding policy violations.

Researchers from the University of Washington and several companies conducted a successful large-scale field trial using poplar trees fortified with a specific probiotic microbe to clean up groundwater contaminated with trichloroethylene (TCE). The study, published in Environmental Science & Technology, found that inoculated trees were healthier, grew more robustly, and reduced TCE levels more effectively than untreated trees. This phytoremediation method offers a lower-cost, sustainable alternative to traditional engineering cleanup methods for Superfund and industrial sites.

Reports citing anonymous U.S. officials state Russian intelligence made repeated contact with President Trump's campaign staff. While U.S. agencies found no proof of collusion, the timing and frequency of the intercepted communications caused concern. President Trump and the Kremlin dismissed the reports. The FBI and Senate Select Committee on Intelligence are investigating Russian election interference and campaign contacts. Some Republicans oppose independent investigations, citing concerns over classified leaks. Three Trump associates—Michael Flynn, Paul Manafort, and Carter Page—left their roles amid allegations of inappropriate Russian contact.

Shi'ite cleric Moqtada al-Sadr set conditions for his followers to surrender weapons used against Islamic State. He demanded that his fighters be given jobs or incorporated into official security forces and that the government support martyrs' families.

To implement a sharded Redis cache on Kubernetes, a StatefulSet is used to deploy three containers with unique DNS names. A Kubernetes Service provides the DNS entries for these replicas, which are then used to configure twemproxy, an open-source proxy developed by Twitter. This configuration is deployed into an ambassador pod via a Kubernetes ConfigMap.

Following the suicide of Assistant Professor Jharna Dalei at Padmanava College of Engineering, security guard Ram Chandra Gouda died of an asthmatic collapse on campus. Police registered an abetment case against an absconding faculty member based on Dalei's suicide note.

Tesla, Inc., a Delaware corporation, filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2020. The company operates in two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of October 20, 2020, there were 947,900,733 shares of common stock outstanding.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2020, Tesla reported total revenues of $20.792 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders of $451 million, compared to $17.194 billion in revenue and a net loss of $967 million for the same period in 2019. Total assets were $45.691 billion and total liabilities were $28.143 billion as of September 30, 2020.

Key corporate activities included a five-for-one stock split in August 2020, a public offering of common stock in February 2020 raising $2.31 billion, and an "at-the-market" offering program in September 2020 that raised $4.97 billion. The company also noted operational disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Researchers investigated the behavior of trace elements in natural zircon single crystals subjected to shock compression at 13.6 and 51.3 GPa. At 13.6 GPa, the zircon phase was retained despite strong fracturing. At 51.3 GPa, the material transformed into textured, mosaic reidite with minor residual zircon. 

Spectroscopic analysis revealed that the transition to reidite significantly decreased cathodoluminescence intensity and shifted the maximum to shorter wavelengths. Notably, the 51.3 GPa sample exhibited bright yellow speckles, indicating the segregation of rare earth elements (REE) on planar defects. The authors suggest this rapid segregation, occurring without prolonged annealing, may be driven by the reconstructive mechanism of the zircon–reidite transition, which expels trivalent trace elements into high-mobility interstitial positions.

This patent application describes improvements to ladar (laser radar) transmitters to optimize "gaze" on specific regions of interest. To address the "fast in the middle" scan characteristic of resonant mirrors, the inventors propose an optical field splitter/inverter (such as a W-shaped reflector or a triangular prism) that redirects the scan so the slower portion resides in the center of the scan area. This can be further enhanced through overlapped inversion to increase dwell time on centerlines.

Additionally, the disclosure introduces induced periodic phase drift for Lissajous scan patterns. By replacing fixed phases with time-varying drift—optimized via a total least squares approach—the system can reduce scan gaps and blindspots in targeted regions. Finally, the application describes a compact beam scanner assembly utilizing an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) reimaging mirror. This design allows two small, equal-sized scanning mirrors to be placed at the ellipsoid's foci, reducing the system's form factor while maintaining beam quality and minimizing field distortions.

This collection of articles and reports details the 2001 California energy crisis, characterized by skyrocketing wholesale electricity and natural gas prices, rolling blackouts, and the bankruptcy of PG&E. Key conflicts include disputes between Governor Gray Davis and President Bush over federal price caps, as well as allegations of market manipulation by energy companies like Enron. Efforts to stabilize the grid include increased conservation, new power contracts (such as GWF Energy's 10-year agreement), and the return of idled plants. Simultaneously, a state Senate committee is subpoenaing energy firms to investigate illegal profiteering.

The White House blocked congressionally approved funding for the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency, effectively shuttering the office. Two senators called for immediate action to reverse the decision.

Nifty is at 10,094 with stop-longs at 10,050 and stop-shorts at 10,200. Bank Nifty is at 24,245 with stop-longs at 24,225 and stop-shorts at 24,450. Short recommendations include Tata Steel (target Rs 567) and Ambuja Cements (target Rs 226), while PowerGrid is recommended long (target Rs 196).
On April 27, 2021, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC to announce its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2021, via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1.

This collection of articles from December 31, 2001, focuses heavily on the collapse of Enron and its broader economic impact. Key reports detail the resulting void in broadband commodity trading, the pressure on SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt to handle the debacle, and the loss of retirement savings for employees and the University of California. Other articles discuss the dangers of overvalued stock prices, the significance of corporate write-offs as distress signals, and the use of retention bonuses during bankruptcies, specifically at Polaroid. Additionally, the text covers electricity producers cutting spending to avoid credit downgrades, 401(k) investor optimism, and various S&P 500 stock performances.

Scientists have developed a theoretical plan called HAMMER to deflect the asteroid Bennu, which has a 1 in 2700 chance of hitting Earth on September 22, 2135. Proposed methods include using a "bulk impactor" or a nuclear device. NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office uses Bennu to test deflection theories and prepare for future threats. Additionally, the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft is traveling to Bennu to map its composition and return a sample to Earth.

The Citi Simplicity® Card features no annual fee, no late fees, and no penalty rates. It offers a 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases. Balance transfers must be completed within four months, with an initial 3% fee (minimum $5) increasing to 5% thereafter. The variable APR following the intro period is 17.99% - 28.74%. The recommended credit score is 670-850.

Rep. Lito Atienza filed House Bill 4758 to replace the MMDA with a Metropolitan Manila Government. The proposed body would consist of a governor, vice governor, and a Metro Manila Council, all elected by the people. Atienza argues that an elected governor would provide the accountability and leadership necessary to implement a master plan for issues like traffic, flooding, and garbage.

Ten-man Manchester City moved to third place after defeating Burnley 2-1. Gael Clichy and substitute Sergio Aguero scored for City, while Ben Mee scored for Burnley. Fernandinho received a red card, resulting in a four-match ban.

Eric Fung, a New York native and former California entrepreneur, moved to Tokyo last year to launch Colega AI. After building startups and restaurants in the US, Fung relocated to Japan, citing the high cost of living and diminished appeal of the Bay Area. His US-registered company employs a remote-first team based in Asia. Fung is currently adjusting to Japanese work culture and the lower cost of living in Tokyo with his wife.

The Consumer Mortgage Coalition is urging the Treasury Department to allow lenders to use the Department of Health and Human Services' National Directory of New Hires to verify income. This alternative would address flaws in the IRS's Income Verification Express System (IVES) to prevent mortgage processing delays. The coalition also requested that the Treasury seek congressional funding to upgrade the IVES system.

CompareCards and other experts highlight various credit cards featuring 0% intro APR offers ranging from 12 to 21 months. Featured options include Discover cards with cashback matches, Bank of America cards with customizable rewards and travel points, Citi cards with balance transfer offers, and Capital One cards providing travel miles and unlimited cash back. Low-interest cards are categorized by fixed or variable APRs, helping consumers reduce borrowing costs.

MLB parks are introducing creative food for 2025, including the Cubs' "Korean corn dog." The Savannah Bananas selection show airs Oct. 9 at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2 and the Banana Ball streaming hub. Stephen A. Smith expressed jubilation over the Yankees' Game 3 win.

Sirius XM (SIRI) has a low-cost capital structure with fixed-rate debt around 4.3% and strong cash flow coverage. Satellite spending cuts are expected to increase free cash flow by roughly 20% by 2026, while share retirements aim to boost ROIC and per-share value. With an ROIC of 11-12% and a WACC of 6%, the company is trading at ~7.6× EV/EBITDA, suggesting a potential 2–3× upside based on unlevered DCF analysis.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces second-generation RT Cores, which double ray/triangle intersection rates and accelerate ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support new data types (TF32, BF16) and a Sparsity feature that can double throughput. The architecture utilizes GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling for increased bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 for faster data transfers, and third-generation NVLink for GPU scaling. 

Additional features include RTX IO for GPU-based asset decompression via Microsoft DirectStorage, HDMI 2.1 support, and hardware-accelerated AV1 decoding via the fifth-generation NVDEC. The architecture is implemented across various products, including the GeForce RTX 30-series, the RTX A6000 workstation GPU, and the A40 data center GPU.

An analysis of the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic found that 3 percent of patients caused over 60 percent of infections. These "superspreaders," often those staying home or the very young and old, drove transmission through traditional funeral practices and caregiving. The epidemic, which killed at least 11,000 people, was stopped via safe burials and quick hospitalization. Similar superspreading events occurred during SARS and MERS outbreaks.

The Automated Fare Collection (AFC) market, valued at $4.81 billion in 2016, is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024. AFC systems automate public transportation ticketing using components like automatic gate, ticket vending, and checking machines. Benefits include increased efficiency, improved transaction rates, reduced queues, and enhanced security. Growth is driven by technological adoption and government investment, though limited smart card use and lack of awareness are restraints. The market is segmented by component, application, technology platform, and geography. Key players include Thales Group, Samsung SDS, and NXP Semiconductors.

Bayhorse Silver Inc. is increasing its non-brokered private placement to 3,000,000 Units at $0.10 per Unit for gross proceeds of $300,000, subject to TSX-V approval. Funds will be used for working capital, equipment acquisition for the Bayhorse Silver Mine, and general administrative costs.

This passage describes methods and systems for small data transmission (SDT) in New Radio (NR) and LTE, focusing on Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) to reduce signaling overhead, latency, and power consumption. It details how user equipment (UE) in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE states can transmit small data via configured grant physical uplink shared channels (PUSCH). To mitigate sequence collisions, the proposed NOMA scheme jointly encodes UE-specific reference bits with information bits using systematic LDPC or Polar encoders. These reference bits serve as preambles or demodulation reference signals (DM-RS) for UE activity detection and channel estimation. The text also outlines specific radio resource configurations, including extended cyclic prefixes and guard bands to support asynchronous transmissions.

The Massachusetts House and Senate passed a supplemental budget bill providing $15 million for school districts educating over 2,300 students who arrived from Puerto Rico following Hurricane Maria. Funds will be distributed based on the number of additional students per district.

After passing a "Jeopardy!" contestant test, John Kizer reflects on the unresolved scientific problem of how memory is stored in the brain. He notes the conflict between theories of localized and generalized storage, mentioning experiments involving rats, humans, and RNA in snails and flatworms. Kizer emphasizes that science often lacks consensus on big ideas.

The Tax Court granted summary judgment for the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, sustaining a determination that the respondent may levy unpaid income taxes assessed against Robert Eugene Poindexter for 1994 and 1996. While the Court rejected the respondent's argument that a taxpayer cannot challenge self-reported liabilities under section 6330(c)(2)(B), it found that the petitioner failed to aver specific facts to show the assessments were inaccurate. The petitioner claimed the returns were incorrect due to royalty disputes with record companies but did not identify specific incorrect income, deductions, or credits. Additionally, the Court found no factual basis for the petitioner's claims regarding procedural errors or improper levy execution.

Acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill approved recommendations allowing individuals over 6 months old to receive updated Covid-19 vaccines after discussing risks and benefits with providers. This allows low-income children in the Vaccines for Children program to access the shots. O’Neill also approved that children under 4 receive the chickenpox shot separately from the combined measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine.

Agents Mutual plans to raise £50 million by floating OnTheMarket.com on London's Alternative Investment Market. The company, Britain's third largest online property site, intends to use the funds to improve technology, customer relations, sales, and a national media campaign to challenge rivals Rightmove and Zoopla.

Police are seeking witnesses after a father was allegedly spat at, punched, and kicked by two men at Coed Bach Park in Pontarddulais on 29 June. The attack occurred after the victim cautioned a moped rider about driving erratically near children.

The court reversed a judgment in favor of an insured plaintiff, ruling that the plaintiff failed to comply with a record-keeping clause in his burglary insurance policies. The clause required records sufficient for the company to accurately determine the amount of loss. The plaintiff maintained a check-cashing fund and recorded only the total amount of cash and checks on a scratch-pad. The court determined that because the fund included checks, the plaintiff was required to keep records listing each check's amount and details necessary to claim against the drawers. Consequently, the plaintiff's failure to maintain these records prevented recovery under the policies.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed a Tax Court judgment holding Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Company, Ltd. liable for income tax deficiencies for 1975 and 1976. Although the taxpayer met the conditions of 26 U.S.C. § 931(a), the court ruled that revenue from sales to its parent company was taxable under section 931(b) because the funds were received within the United States via deposits into a Honolulu bank account.

This work examines the application of steady-state global variance reduction techniques (VRTs)—including implicit capture (IC), weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and the Cooper-Larsen (CL) method—to time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations. It specifically explores the interactions between these VRTs and population control techniques (PCTs), namely uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC).

Testing using the Shift and MC/DC codes across three scenarios (Pulsed Slab, AZURV1, and 1D SCRAM) indicates that FW-CADIS and CL weight windows can improve efficiency, with time-dependent weight windows performing better than static ones. Results show that combining weight windows with WC leads to memory exhaustion due to excessive particle splitting. Additionally, IC demonstrated poor synergy with UC. Conversely, the combination of CL weight windows and UC proved highly effective for global variance reduction.

To address declining language enrollment in the U.S., this article proposes an "imagined communities" approach to language education. This method uses task-based instruction to create authentic scenarios—such as planning a move to a target-language city—allowing students to imagine themselves interacting with target cultures. By focusing on the connecting power of language, educators can increase student interest, retention, and feelings of membership within target-language communities across all educational levels.

The National Endowment for the Humanities and the First Nations Development Institute are each contributing approximately $2 million to fund Native American language revitalization programs. About 15 programs will be funded annually through a competitive process prioritizing immersion or language retention and restoration efforts.

On May 3, 2001, several energy-related reports were released. Allegheny Energy purchased three Midwest power plants from Enron for $667 million. In India, Enron's Dabhol Power Company faced a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, leading Indian banks to seek government intervention and the scheduling of a meeting with a government panel. 

In California, officials considered a buyer's boycott to lower electricity costs despite potential economic risks. Meanwhile, the Democratic National Committee criticized President Bush's energy policy as being influenced by special interests. Other news included Innogy starting power trading in mainland Europe, Mosaic Group reporting strong first-quarter results, and Scottish Power restructuring to focus on energy. Additionally, European phone companies showed improved debt-repayment abilities, and European corporates increased their use of credit derivatives.

This disclosure provides methods, polypeptides, nucleic acids, and genetically modified host cells for producing cannabinoids, cannabinoid precursors, and their derivatives. It identifies novel geranyl pyrophosphate:olivetolic acid geranyltransferase (GOT) polypeptides, such as CsPT4 and its truncated version CsPT4t, which catalyze the production of cannabigerolic acid (CBGA) from GPP and olivetolic acid at rates at least ten times higher than previously known Cannabis polypeptides. These GOT polypeptides exhibit broad substrate specificity, enabling the bioproduction of both naturally occurring and non-naturally occurring cannabinoids in vivo or in vitro. The disclosure also details the use of various other polypeptides, including TKS, OAC, and cannabinoid synthases, to construct metabolic pathways in host cells (such as yeast or plant cells) to convert simple feedstocks into high-value cannabinoids.

James T. Hodgkinson, a former Bernie Sanders volunteer, shot Louisiana Congressman Steve Scalise and three others during a congressional baseball practice. Scalise is in critical condition. Rep. Garret Graves and other Republicans attribute the attack to a divisive political climate and rhetoric. Sanders and President Trump have both condemned the violence and called for unity.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2019. For the three months ended September 30, 2019, the company reported total net sales of $69.981 billion and net income of $2.134 billion. For the nine months ended September 30, 2019, net sales were $193.086 billion with net income of $8.320 billion. The company operates through three segments: North America, International, and AWS. As of September 30, 2019, total assets were $199.099 billion and total stockholders' equity was $56.508 billion.

An Ilorin Magistrates’ Court remanded Shehu Abubakar and Abdulkareem Maikudi for allegedly killing Musa Kareem following a dispute over a cell phone. The accused face charges of criminal conspiracy and culpable homicide. The court adjourned the case until July 12 to allow for further police investigation.

The speaker felt energized throughout a game featuring many powerplays and penalty kills. They attributed the team's strength to having four scoring lines. Despite both teams playing well defensively and the ice becoming chippy, the speaker scored a goal after Sergei provided an open lane. The team maintained composure between periods to eventually find an opening.

A New York Times survey of 65 federal judges revealed widespread dissatisfaction with the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions regarding President Trump's second term. Only 12 judges felt the docket was used appropriately or provided sufficient guidance to lower courts, and 42 believed it harmed public perception of the judiciary. While some judges described the situation as a "judicial crisis," one Trump appointee viewed the orders as "flushing out anti-democratic rulings." The Volokh Conspiracy critiqued the survey, suggesting it may have oversampled unhappy judges.

The January 15, 2002, Energy Central Direct daily edition reports on various energy sector developments. Key stories include the imminent U.S. clearance of UK Grid's Nimo bid, UBS sharing profits from an Enron unit, and the Senate Banking Committee scheduling an Enron hearing. Other news covers utility deregulation in Texas and Ohio, energy mergers in the EU, and various international power projects and regulatory issues.

Nigeria launched its National Cancer Control Plan 2018-2022 to improve access to equitable diagnostics, treatment, and drugs.
