A state department of public instruction assessment in Karnataka revealed that over 10 lakh students in government and aided schools from Classes 4-9 require remedial classes, with approximately 4.5 lakh needing help in Mathematics and Science. The Students Achievement Survey involved over 36 lakh students across 50,000 schools.

Auckland Airport's international terminal resumed operations after police and Aviation Security located a woman who entered the terminal with a knife. The security breach caused screening delays and affected at least four Air New Zealand and Virgin Australia flights.

A study in Choma District, southern Zambia, used amplicon deep-sequencing on samples collected from 2018 to 2023 to monitor antimalarial drug resistance. The WHO-candidate Pfk13 P441L mutation, associated with artemisinin resistance, was found in 6% of all samples, increasing from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023. This exceeds the WHO's 5% concern threshold. Additionally, the Pfk13 A578S mutation was identified in 0.6% of 2023 samples, and MDR1 Y184F prevalence was 41%.

U.S. stocks rose Monday, while oil and gold prices fell. New York Fed President William Dudley expects another 2017 rate rise. Eurozone factory output declined in June, China's economy slowed in July, and Japan's GDP grew 4.0% in the April-June quarter. Canada seeks a more progressive NAFTA. Additionally, Federal Reserve research found the natural unemployment rate has remained stable over the last century.

This study examined factors affecting the attraction and retention of special education teachers in rural remote Midwest US locales. Surveying 93 teachers, the research identified four primary themes: financial incentives, provision of support, job-related factors, and rural initiatives. Results indicated that financial incentives (such as increased salary) are the strongest attractors (96%), while provision of support from administrators and colleagues is most critical for retention (70%). Job-related factors, specifically reducing paperwork and caseloads, and rural initiatives like "Grow Your Own" programs also play roles. The study found a significant positive correlation between perceived support, job satisfaction, and the intent to remain in the profession.

On December 22, NASA's Suomi NPP satellite captured an infrared image of the aurora borealis over several northern Canadian regions. These lights occur when solar wind particles interact with Earth's magnetic field and atmosphere, releasing photons of various colors. While occurring anytime, the most magnificent displays happen roughly every 11 years.

Nintendo announced the development of Mario Kart Tour, a mobile app expected to be released between April 2018 and March 2019. This follows Nintendo's release of other smartphone games including Super Mario Run, Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp, and Fire Emblem Heroes.

Tyreek Hill underwent surgery to repair a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL. His agent stated the surgery went well and Hill is expected to play next season. The Dolphins are adapting to his season-ending injury by utilizing other players and signing wide receiver Wilson to the practice squad.

Thomas H. Fisher appealed a summary judgment granted to Homer P. Hargrave and the partnership Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane. Fisher sought an accounting for losses from transactions with Fuller, Rodney & Co., alleging that the defendants succeeded to that firm's business and assumed its liabilities.

The court affirmed the summary judgment, finding no issue of fact. Affidavits from Hargrave and former Fuller partner Byron G. Webster, along with a written agreement, established that the defendants did not merge with or assume the liabilities of Fuller, Rodney & Co., and that Fisher's account was not transferred. The court disregarded Fisher's opposing affidavit as it was based on information and belief rather than competent evidence. Additionally, the court found no record of a denied motion for discovery and determined that the equitable action for accounting fell within the provisions of the Civil Practice Act.
BAE Systems agreed to sell 24 Typhoon fighter planes to Qatar in a 6 billion pound deal. The agreement includes training, support, and missiles and bombs from MBDA Missile Systems and Raytheon.

USD/JPY rallied after a North Korean missile test, reaching 114.17 before easing. While the Nikkei rose 0.5%, traders favored long positions with bids at 113.85-75 and offers at 114.20/30. Order flows will drive price swings as no U.S. data is expected.

Microsoft Corporation is a global technology company focused on a "mobile-first, cloud-first" strategy. Its operations are divided into three reportable segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, Server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Devices, Gaming, Search advertising). The company develops and sells software, services, and hardware across more than 190 countries. A study by Osaka Metropolitan University found that Tokyo residents with longer commutes experience increased insomnia and daytime sleepiness, while smaller housing sizes also predict insomnia. For homes meeting the 95 m² standard, commutes exceeding 52 minutes reached the insomnia cutoff. Researchers suggest that housing planning considering the trade-off between location and size could improve sleep health.

A proper 1v1 soccer defending stance involves one foot forward and one back, typically with the dominant leg as the trail foot. For adults, feet are generally separated by 18 inches on a 30-degree angle, with knees bent and weight on the balls of the feet. This balanced position allows defenders to react quickly, slow the opponent, and prepare for tackles. Stance is modified by field location: the left foot leads on the right side and the right foot leads on the left side to force attackers toward the sideline. Training involves practicing these positions at increasing speeds and maintaining a "goal side" location.

The Iso play is a downhill running scheme used in I-formation and pro-style offenses. It utilizes a fullback as an isolated lead blocker against a linebacker, supported by base blocks and double teams. Its strengths include speed and simplicity, though it depends heavily on powerful personnel. Variations include Shotgun Iso and Weakside Iso.

GBPJPY is a minor cross currency pair comparing the British pound (base currency) to the Japanese yen (quote currency). It is formed by trading GBPUSD and USDJPY. Known as "Geppy" or "The Beast," it reflects economic health in Western Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.

Intraday trading is best during the Asian (23:00 to 06:00 GMT) and London (08:00 to 16:00 GMT) sessions. GBPJPY and USDJPY can occasionally show a high positive correlation. While the author considers forex trading difficult due to its zero-sum nature and unpredictability, they suggest that backtesting is essential to find profitable strategies and diversification.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines SD Memory Cards, categorized by capacity: Standard (up to 2GB), High (up to 32GB), and Extended (up to 2TB). Cards are either Read/Write or Read-Only (ROM).

The specification details various bus speed modes, including Default Speed, High Speed, and Ultra High Speed (UHS-I and UHS-II). UHS-I supports 1.8V signaling and speeds up to 104MB/sec, while UHS-II introduces a second interface row for full-duplex modes reaching up to 624MB/s (UHS-III).

Communication is host-controlled via broadcast or addressed commands. The process involves card identification mode (using CMD0, CMD8, and ACMD41) and data transfer mode. Data is transferred in blocks, protected by CRC.

Write protection is managed through mechanical switches, internal card settings, or password protection. The Card Ownership Protection (COP) feature provides advanced security using PWD and Force Erase Passwords (FEP) to manage card access and ownership.

Presidential Spokesman Harry Roque stated that President Rodrigo Duterte will investigate allegations against Development Academy of the Philippines President Elba Cruz. DAP employees accused Cruz of unauthorized restructuring, CSC rule violations, threatening mass terminations, and frequent foreign travel. Additionally, Duterte plans to fire all top officials of the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor over alleged unnecessary junkets and failure to meet en banc.

This study analyzes various educational leadership models, including administrative/managerial, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent, and participative styles. The research finds that no single model can fully address the evolving needs of school organizations due to their respective strengths and limitations. The University of Windsor Board of Governors appointed Douglas Kneale as interim president and vice-chancellor starting July 1. Kneale, the current provost and vice-president academic, will serve until a successor to Alan Wildeman is found. Wildeman will soon announce an acting provost.

Ipswich mayoral by-election candidates have received nearly $60,000 in donations, reported via the Electoral Commission Queensland's new real-time disclosure system. Councillor Andrew Antoniolli received $46,400, including a $15,000 donation from Plencove. This passage describes methods and apparatus for improving 3D sound localization, specifically addressing the difficulty listeners have in localizing binaural sounds in the "near-field" range (less than one meter). To resolve this and reduce computational complexity, the system convolves sound using far-field Head Related Transfer Functions (HRTFs) to position the sound at a coordinate location behind the actual sound source or image. Because listeners associate sound with visible objects, they perceive the audio as originating from the near-field source even though it is processed to a far-field location on a line-of-sight.

The system can also adjust sound volume to match the near-field distance and handle multiple sound sources by assigning distinct far-field coordinates to different images. Additionally, the technology allows users to switch between binaural and mono/stereo sound via portable electronic device actions, such as rotating the device, changing head orientation, or using sensors to detect the presence or gaze of the listener.

The professor discusses orthonormal expansions, moving from finite to infinite dimensions. He explains that projecting a vector onto a set of orthonormal functions allows for closer approximation of the original vector, a principle applicable to all orthonormal expansions, including Fourier series. He notes that while Fourier series approximate waveforms, proving the remaining difference goes to zero is difficult; however, this difference must be orthogonal to the starting functions.

The lecture introduces prolate spheroidal functions, which maximize energy concentration within fixed time and bandwidth intervals, solving the problem of time- and frequency-limiting.

Transitioning to communication channels, the professor describes the process of converting binary data to symbols, then to signals, and finally to waveforms. He emphasizes "layering," where discrete encoding and modulation are treated as separate problems to simplify system design.

In modulation, the professor explains Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM), where binary digits are mapped to equispaced real-number signals. To convert these signals into waveforms, a filter is used. While the sinc function is ideal for avoiding intersymbol interference (ISI), it is impractical due to causality and infinite delay.

The professor introduces the Nyquist criterion, which defines the conditions for a composite filter (transmitter and receiver filters combined) to avoid ISI. He explains that "ideal Nyquist" filters must satisfy specific band-edge symmetry in the frequency domain. To balance bandwidth and delay, practical systems often use a "raised cosine filter," which decays faster than a sinc function.

This study investigates whether rutile $\text{RuO}_2$ intrinsically hosts altermagnetism, specifically examining the origin of exchange bias (EB) observed in $\text{RuO}_2/\text{FM}$ heterostructures. Using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron diffraction (PND), and polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR), the researchers found that sputtered $\text{RuO}_2$ thin films lack a detectable sublattice moment, indicating they are not intrinsically altermagnetic in their ground state.

Analysis of $\text{RuO}_2/\text{Fe}$ heterostructures via atom probe tomography (APT), HRTEM, and EELS revealed that the EB effect is driven by a chemically intermixed reaction interlayer containing magnetite ($\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$) formed due to the high oxidation potential of Fe relative to Ru. This conclusion is supported by the absence of EB in $\text{RuO}_2/\text{Ni}$ heterostructures and the presence of EB in $\text{Fe}/\text{Ru}$ bilayers lacking $\text{RuO}_2$. The results establish that EB in these systems arises from interfacial moment pinning rather than intrinsic magnetic ordering in $\text{RuO}_2$.

This paper proposes a probabilistic computational model of implicature comprehension based on relevance-theoretic pragmatics, implemented using the ProbLog language. The authors argue that human cognition maximizes relevance—defined as the balance between positive cognitive effects and processing effort—and that overtly intentional communication conveys a presumption of optimal relevance.

The model treats comprehension as a "fast and frugal" heuristic where listeners sample interpretive hypotheses in order of accessibility, stopping at the first that satisfies their relevance expectations. To formalize this, the authors use Bayesian networks to model the parallel adjustment of explicatures, implicit premises, and implicatures. They conceptualize the utility of an utterance through the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between a listener's prior and posterior probability distributions over manifest propositions.

The authors test the model using five interpretive hypotheses, demonstrating that the "winning" interpretation is one that satisfies relevance expectations while maximizing KL divergence and minimizing the size of the Herbrand base (representing processing effort). The resulting "as-if-optimization" model provides a quantitative tool for investigating the heuristic nature of relevance-guided communication.

Russ Tedrake introduces "Underactuated Robotics," a course focusing on machines that utilize natural dynamics rather than overriding them with high-gain feedback. He contrasts conservative, fully actuated systems like ASIMO with agile, underactuated examples found in nature, such as birds, bats, and fish. 

Tedrake defines a system as underactuated if its control input cannot accelerate it in every direction (the rank of the input matrix is less than the dimension of the coordinates). He argues that most unsolved robotics problems—including walking, flying, and manipulation—are underactuated. The course will use a computational approach, applying optimal control, reinforcement learning, and motion planning to model systems like the simple pendulum, the Acrobot, and compass gait walkers.

Nick Mathewson, a Tor developer, discusses the anonymity network, which uses approximately 6,000 volunteer nodes to provide privacy for millions of users. He explains that anonymity is the inability of an observer to link a participant to an action, distinguishing it from unobservability and unlinkability. Tor employs onion routing, where traffic is encrypted in layers and passed through multiple relays to prevent any single party from correlating the user with their destination.

Mathewson addresses the use of Tor by criminals, arguing that effective security systems are inevitably used by bad actors. He describes the technical challenges of maintaining a large user base to ensure anonymity, the use of directory authorities for node discovery, and the implementation of hidden services for responder anonymity. He concludes by discussing common attacks, such as traffic correlation and application-level leaks, and outlines future goals, including revamping cryptography and improving scalability.

Saving penalty kicks is a challenging task for goalkeepers, with save rates generally under 15%. Violations by the goalkeeper may result in retakes or cautions.

Coaches should provide positive support and specialized training, emphasizing a "read and react" approach over guessing. Goalkeepers can improve by studying cues such as ball placement, approach angle, run-up, plant foot, hip orientation, and chin direction. Mental preparation involves visualization, positive self-talk, controlled breathing, and consistent pre-shot routines. Physical preparation requires agility, proper equipment, and research on opposing players' tendencies.

During the kick, goalkeepers are encouraged to maintain composure, use intimidating but legal tactics to distract the kicker, and avoid diving prematurely. After the kick, they must react quickly to rebounds or initiate fast breaks. Coaches may also utilize tactical positioning, such as standing slightly off-center, to influence the kicker's perception of the goal.

Metagenomic binning clusters fragmented DNA reads into distinct genomes to enable biological analysis. Traditional methods use k-mer profiles to create deterministic embeddings, but these struggle with sequences shared between species (e.g., via horizontal gene transfer) or distinct sequences with similar k-mer profiles.

To address these limitations, the authors propose UNCERTAINGEN, a framework using probabilistic embeddings. Instead of mapping fragments to single points, it maps them to distributions to encode ambiguity and uncertainty. This approach utilizes a contrastive-learning formulation with closed-form expressions for efficient optimization. The authors provide theoretical analysis on embedding distinguishability and empirically demonstrate that this probabilistic method outperforms deterministic k-mer and LLM-based embeddings on real metagenomic datasets.

Graph limits provide an analytic framework to represent the limit of a sequence of graphs as a single object called a graphon. A graphon is defined as a symmetric, measurable function from the unit square to the interval [0, 1]. 

The theory defines convergence based on homomorphism densities; a sequence of graphs converges if the homomorphism density of every fixed graph $H$ converges. This is equivalent to convergence in a metric space defined by the "cut distance," which utilizes the cut norm to measure the difference between graphons while accounting for vertex rearrangements via measure-preserving transformations.

Three main theorems form the basis of this theory:
1. Convergence in homomorphism densities is equivalent to being a Cauchy sequence under the cut distance.
2. Every convergent sequence of graphs or graphons has a limit graphon.
3. The space of graphons is compact, a result philosophically and mathematically linked to Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma.

The AGESA™ software core provides a set of procedures and libraries for host environments to initialize AMD processor components. It supports two build methods: binary modules (indirect) and source integration. In UEFI environments, execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP phases, utilizing specific Microsoft assembler and compiler tools.

Key operational requirements include:
*   **Stack Management:** The host must establish a stack environment using provided macros like `AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK` and remove it via `AMD_DISABLE_UEFI_STACK` once main memory is available.
*   **Call-Out Interface:** A host-implemented router function dispatches AGESA call-outs using a standard header and function identifiers.
*   **Initialization Sequence:**
    *   `AmdInitReset`: Performs minimal basic processor initialization and allocates execution cache.
    *   `AmdInitEarly`: Establishes the program environment and configures platform-specific operational characteristics.
    *   `AmdInitPost`: Initializes system memory and transitions the boot from pre-memory to post-memory phase.
    *   `AmdInitEnv`: Performs graphics display hardware configuration.
    *   `AmdInitLate`: Generates informational data tables (ACPI, DMI) for the operating system.
*   **Power Management:** `AmdInitRtb` saves silicon registers for suspend mode, while `AmdInitResume` and `AmdInitRestore` handle the resume boot path.
*   **Required Host Functions:** The host must implement `AgesaAllocateBuffer` for memory allocation, `AgesaDeallocateBuffer` for memory release, and a system reset function.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) in Chile, with observations starting in 2026. The project includes two instruments: Mod-Cam, a cryogenic testbed, and Prime-Cam, the primary science instrument. Additionally, testing identified that elevated inter-channel crosstalk originated in the SMP-SMA transition PCBs rather than the striplines. A redesigned PCB using impedance-matched vias is expected to improve isolation by approximately 20 dB, meeting project requirements.

The Inverted Hammer is a bullish reversal candlestick pattern occurring at the bottom of downtrends or pullbacks in uptrends. It features a small real body at the lower end, a long upper shadow, and little to no lower shadow, indicating that buyers are gaining momentum. While a green body is more bullish than a red one, both can signal a reversal.

Traders use the pattern to identify potential upswings and enter long positions, often combining it with support levels, trendlines, moving averages, and momentum oscillators for confirmation. Strategies include swing trading in uptrends and mean reversion in oversold markets. Key risk management involves using stop-loss orders and position sizing.

Backtests on the S&P 500 show the pattern is profitable with a win ratio between 53% and 65% and an average gain of 0.36% per trade. It differs from the Shooting Star, which forms at the top of upward swings and signals a bearish reversal. Disadvantages include subjectivity and the potential for false signals.

This paper analyzes the optimal pricing policy for a monopolist selling a single expiring item to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically. Formulated as a Stackelberg game, the model assigns time-sensitive utility to the seller—who faces total loss upon expiration—while buyers are temporally neutral, balancing potential price drops against the risk of stockout.

The authors first introduce "Value-Based Threshold strategies" to decouple buyer valuation from arrival time, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions to prove the existence and uniqueness of equilibrium in a continuous valuation setting. Second, they derive pricing schedules for two market regimes: a constant price for "thin" markets (low arrival rates) to prevent strategic delaying, and a linear discounting schedule for "thick" markets (high arrival rates) where intense competition renders buyers myopic. Numerical simulations further indicate that optimal schedules shift from end-loaded to flat to front-loaded based on the seller's level of time sensitivity.

*   **Digital Architectural Elements (DAEs) and Wall Interfaces:** Modular units installed on structural elements (like mullions) containing sensors (light, audio, air quality, thermal), processors, and peripherals (speakers, displays, antennas).

The system enables integrated environmental monitoring and control. Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) allows customers to co-sign update packages using 2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA keys provided during early boot. Update packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware portions, and are non-persistent across reboots. 

The process requires a customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent to create a 2MB aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER in DRAM, append the co-signing header, the AMD update package, and the signature. The ASP then protects the DRAM address, verifies signatures, executes the patch, and updates the patch level. 

Specific requirements include:
* **SEV/SNP:** SEV updates prevent rollback; SNP requires HV-FIXED pages via the RMPUPDATE command.
* **Resiliency:** Packages must verify existing firmware versions before applying to avoid system resets.
* **Commands:** `GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO` retrieves current patch and firmware levels, while `UPDATE_FW` loads and executes the package.
* **Naming:** Packages follow the format `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg`.

This course on combinatorial theory explores the relationship between graph theory and additive combinatorics. The instructor uses Schur's Theorem—which states that any finite coloring of positive integers contains a monochromatic solution to $x + y = z$—to demonstrate this connection. The theorem is proven by applying Ramsey's Theorem for triangles to a complete graph where edge colors are derived from the integers.

The lecture also provides a historical overview of additive combinatorics, highlighting milestones such as Van der Waerden's Theorem and Szemerédi's Theorem regarding arithmetic progressions in sets of positive density. These results led to diverse mathematical approaches, including ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis, and hypergraph regularity. Further extensions include the multi-dimensional Szemerédi Theorem, the polynomial Szemerédi Theorem, and the Green-Tao Theorem, which proves that primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. The course will conclude by examining extremal graph theory and the specific graph-theoretic problems related to Roth's Theorem.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command processes 1-128 migration entries to move pages, updating IOMMU host PTEs. In SNP-enabled systems, it is restricted to Hypervisor-owned pages. For non-SNP systems, software must manage ATS devices and CPU access before calling the command. 2M pages must be smashed into 4K pages. Firmware validates addresses and page states, manages TLB invalidations, and copies data while maintaining encryption.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST command moves 1-128 SNP guest pages. It requires RMP_ENFORCE to be 1 and source pages to be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, while destination pages must be Pre-Migration. DMA is not supported. 2M pages must be 2M aligned and physically contiguous 4K pages.

A separate command marks the end of migration sequences and can trigger interrupts. Errors are reported via command status, migration list entries, the PM_STATUS register, or the Machine Check Architecture (MCA). Hardware errors may render all pages in a batch unrecoverable.

SOS pressure defense requires commitment, repetitive drills, and positive coaching to build player tenacity. The "On-ball" system consists of SET (forcing the ballhandler to dribble), ON (guiding the dribbler to a checkpoint), and SMOTHER (applying maximum pressure to prevent shooting or passing). "Off-ball" pressure utilizes SNUGGLE (denying passes), OFF (denying cuts to the basket), and STRIKE (weakside help and impeding entry into the three-second area). A study of 3,395 computer science-allied course syllabi from the top 100 NIRF-ranked engineering institutions in India found that only 2.21% (75 courses) incorporated AI ethics. Most of these courses addressed the topic superficially, with 60% dedicating only one session to it, while only 7% were fully devoted to AI ethics. 

Commonly covered themes included privacy, legal aspects, and data governance (42%), accountability and policies (32%), and ethical frameworks (24%). However, topics like generative AI concerns (11%) and social impact (8%) were less frequent. The analysis revealed a lack of dedicated instructional resources, as over 90% of courses relied on standard technical textbooks, and no courses had documented assessments specifically for AI ethics. The authors conclude that AI ethics remains marginally and inconsistently integrated into Indian computing education, highlighting a need for structured pedagogical design and open curricular access.

The invention describes a system and method for real-time rendering of computer-generated graphics that reduces computing resource usage during saccades. By using sensors—such as optical, EMG, or Doppler sensors—the system detects the onset of a saccade and the resulting saccadic masking. Saved resources may be reallocated to low-frequency updates, such as complex lighting calculations, or used to reduce power consumption. The system may utilize an eye movement model, calibrated for individual users, to predict saccade duration and determine the extent of resource reduction.

Researchers used the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method (IVBM) to grow bulk $\text{MnBi}_2\text{Te}_4/(\text{Bi}_2\text{Te}_3)_n$ crystals, identifying four growth stages: turbulent flow, rapid $\text{MnTe}$ precipitation, stationary flow, and cessation of flow. These stages dictate the stacking of septuple layers (SLs) and quintuple layers (QLs). 

Results show that SL spacing is inversely related to $\text{MnTe}$ supersaturation due to diffusion-limited competition. Samples with closely spaced, $\text{Mn}$-rich SLs (Samples A and B) exhibit antiferromagnetic behavior, while those with larger SL separations and $\text{Mn}$ depletion (Samples C and D) show ferromagnetic behavior. The study concludes that controlling melt composition and flow dynamics allows for the tuning of structural and magnetic properties in these topological materials.

This document describes a neuromodulation system and method designed to deliver a linear electric field to neural tissue, specifically targeting the dorsal horn (DH) or dorsal root (DR) while minimizing activation of the dorsal column (DC). The system comprises electrodes on one or more leads, a neural modulation generator, and a programming system.

The programming system determines electrode fractionalizations based on a "target multipole," which uses at least three target poles to progressively stack fractionalizations. This configuration creates a wider electric field and reduces the second-order spatial derivative of voltage, which preferentially modulates DH/DR tissue over DC tissue to provide pain relief without inducing paresthesia.

The system may include a user interface to adjust the target multipole's angle, focus, and spread, or automatically determine the multipole based on user-drawn anatomical regions or identified pain areas. Additional features include the use of directional electrodes, flanking electrodes for current steering or edge guarding, and search heuristics to optimize the electric field.
